name: GitHub Copilot in VS Code (agent mode hooks)

versions_seen.where: VS Code app (Copilot harness); the tester ran the scripted agent-mode session by hand at 18:10 EDT in a scratch folder with a repo .github/hooks probe (probe:versions/1.140.0/)

cocheck_relevance: CoCheck shares the Copilot CLI profile and install file for VS Code agent mode (VS Code reading ~/.copilot/hooks is documented, not probed: copilot-vscode-reads-user-hooks-unverified). Calls inside a subagent carry no agentId and arrive under the subagent's own sessionId: CoCheck links them to the main session by the launching task call's prompt, else holds them until the main session's subagentStop names the helper (src/copilot-helpers.ts), and drops them when the main session is untracked.

available.claim: VS Code agent mode runs Copilot hooks; the page is marked Preview.
available.note: Not run on this Mac; nothing probed.

config.claim: The VS Code Copilot harness reads ~/.copilot/hooks ($COPILOT_HOME), .github/hooks/*.json, inline hooks in .github/copilot/settings(.local).json and ~/.copilot/settings.json, repo .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json, plugins and agent frontmatter hooks.
Whether VS Code also reads ~/.claude/settings.json: not listed on the page.
VS Code has a separate 'Claude session target' with its own hook implementation that uses Claude Code's own config.
VS Code 1.140.0 loaded and ran a repo .github/hooks probe in a scratch folder (workspace-level hooks work in agent mode).
config.note: Folder was opened by hand in the tester's VS Code; workspace trust and tool approvals were clicked through.

config.claim: Whether VS Code reads ~/.copilot/hooks was not tested (it would need the directory in the tester's real home); the page lists it.

The older VS Code Local harness has eight events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, Stop, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, PreCompact) on a different schema, for migration only; it explains older material listing fewer events.

trust_or_approval.claim: Claude and Codex harnesses are disabled when enterprise-managed Copilot settings apply.

fact.claim: sessionStart fired in VS Code 1.140.0 agent mode with the CLI's camelCase payload (sessionId, timestamp, cwd, source, initialPrompt).
fact.note: can_block, can_rewrite, timeout (30 s) and matcher are inherited from the shared GitHub reference and were not tested in VS Code; whether VS Code honors `matcher` is unverified (no page read 2026-10-24 says it is ignored, which an earlier register entry claimed). Order differs from the CLI: sessionStart fired after userPromptSubmitted and userPromptTransformed in VS Code.

fact.claim: permissionRequest fired in VS Code 1.140.0 for edit and bash (hookName, toolName, toolInput, permissionSuggestions); inside a subagent it keeps the parent sessionId.
fact.note: Blocking inherited from the CLI reference, untested here.

fact.claim: notification fired in VS Code 1.140.0 with notification_type permission_prompt, title 'Permission needed', hook_event_name "Notification" (camelCase payload otherwise).

fact.claim: postToolUseFailure is documented in the shared GitHub reference; VS Code 1.140.0 did not fire it in the probe (no tool-level failure occurred, the failing shell command arrived as postToolUse success).

fact.claim: errorOccurred is documented in the shared GitHub reference; not fired in the VS Code 1.140.0 probe.

missing_events.claim: postToolUseFailure and errorOccurred were not seen in VS Code 1.140.0 and no source says VS Code lacks them; listed as events with status unverified. The earlier register list of five 'missing' events was wrong for userPromptTransformed, permissionRequest and notification, which fire live.
missing_events.note: The VS Code page names nine events and defers to the GitHub reference for the rest (documentation lag; VS Code 1.141 to 1.143 release notes have no hook items).

config_paths.claim: Repo scope, Claude Code's files: .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json.

surfaces.claim: VS Code agent mode ran command hooks (observed 1.140.0, repo .github/hooks); the page marks the feature Preview.
surfaces.note: An earlier entry said the VS Code parser ignores matcher values; no page read 2026-10-24 says so and it was not tested, so matcher handling is unverified.

surfaces.claim: VS Code Claude session target: runs Claude Code's own hook implementation, not Copilot's.

sandbox_and_network.claim: Hooks wrote a file under HOME outside the workspace and reached 127.0.0.1 (HTTP 200) on every one of 36 calls in VS Code 1.140.0 agent mode.
sandbox_and_network.note: Whether VS Code has a sandbox setting that would change this was not tested.

other_observation_channels.claim: VS Code chat session JSON under workspaceStorage (chatSessions): from memory, no official page read.

call_ids.claim: No per-call id is documented for the shared Copilot hook payload; VS Code input beyond the shared reference was not read.
No tool call id in any of the 36 VS Code 1.140.0 hook payloads; id-like fields are sessionId, and agentId only at subagentStop.

helpers_or_subagents.claim: subagentStart and subagentStop fired for both the custom agent `writer` and the built-in general-purpose agent (task tool) in VS Code 1.140.0, contradicting the docs for the built-in agent.

Subagent attribution differs from the CLI: calls inside a subagent carry no agentId or parentAgentId; they arrive under the subagent's own sessionId (userPromptSubmitted, userPromptTransformed, preToolUse, postToolUse, agentStop). The link to the parent appears only at subagentStop (its agentId equals that inner sessionId, its sessionId is the parent's) or earlier through permissionRequest, which keeps the parent sessionId. subagentStart carries no id.
helpers_or_subagents.note: For default-off tracking the inner calls arrive under a session id CoCheck has never seen, so they must be held until the subagent links back.

open_questions: Does VS Code read ~/.copilot/hooks? Not tested (needs the directory in the tester's real home).
Does VS Code honor `matcher`? Untested; the earlier 'ignored' claim had no source.
preCompact, postToolUseFailure and errorOccurred did not fire in the 1.140.0 probe; blocking, rewriting and timeout behavior in VS Code are inherited from the CLI reference, untested.
Does a VS Code sandbox setting change hook write or network access?
Other IDEs (JetBrains, Xcode): hooks not found.
MCP config paths for VS Code (.vscode/mcp.json, user mcp.json) are from memory, not read.
